questions.question: Efficient and rapid movement of goods, services, and people over space is a prerequisite for fast development. Hence, which sector is termed as the 'lifeline' of a national economy?
questions.explanation: Transport, communication, and trade are complementary to each other. Together, they facilitate economic exchange, integrate distant regions, and act as the lifelines of our economy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key operational advantage of roadways over railways?
options: Roadways provide door-to-door service and the cost of loading/unloading is much lower
Roadways can transport thousands of tonnes of iron ore in a single trip cheaper than trains
Roadways do not require any construction or maintenance capital
Roadways cannot be built on undulating hilly terrains
questions.explanation: Road transport provides door-to-door service, thus the cost of loading and unloading is much lower. Roads can also negotiate higher gradients of slopes and can traverse dissected mountains like the Himalayas.

questions.question: The Golden Quadrilateral Super Highway project links which four major mega cities of India with 6-lane highways?
questions.explanation: The government launched the Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways project connecting Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai-Mumbai and Delhi by 6-lane super highways. It is implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

questions.question: The North-South Corridor connects Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) with which southern coastal terminus?
questions.explanation: The North-South corridor links Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) and Kanniyakumari (Tamil Nadu), while the East-West corridor connects Silchar (Assam) and Porbandar (Gujarat).

questions.question: National Highways (NH) that link extreme parts of the country are constructed and maintained by which government agency?
questions.explanation: National Highways are the primary road systems and are laid and maintained by the Central Public Works Department (CPWD).

questions.question: The historical highway between Delhi and Amritsar, known as Sher Shah Suri Marg, is officially designated as:
questions.explanation: The historical Sher-Shah Suri Marg is called National Highway No. 1, between Delhi and Amritsar.

questions.question: In which year was the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) established to develop roads of strategic importance in the northern and north-eastern border areas?
questions.explanation: Border Roads Organisation (BRO), a Government of India undertaking, was established in 1960 for the development of the roads of strategic importance in the northern and north-eastern border areas.

questions.question: The northern plains of India have the highest railway network density primarily due to:
options: Abundance of high mountain passes and gorges
Dense evergreen forest reserves and marshy terrain
Presence of dry desert dunes without vegetation
Vast level land, high population density, and rich agricultural resources
questions.explanation: The northern plains with their vast level land, high population density and rich agricultural resources provided the most favorable condition for the growth of railway network.

questions.question: The development of the Konkan Railway along the western coast of India facilitated passenger and freight travel, but has faced challenges such as:
options: Total absence of rivers requiring bridges
Sinking of tracks in some stretches and severe landslides during monsoons
Extreme freezing temperatures causing tracks to crack in summer
questions.explanation: Along the western coast, the Konkan railway has facilitated movement of passengers and goods. However, it has also faced problems such as sinking of track in some stretches and landslides during monsoon seasons.

questions.question: Which of the following commodities is transported via underground pipelines after being converted into a slurry?
questions.explanation: Pipelines transport crude oil, petroleum products, and natural gas. Solids can also be transported through a pipeline when converted into slurry, such as iron ore slurry from Kudremukh to Mangaluru.

questions.question: The famous 1,700-km long cross-country Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline links gas fields in Gujarat to fertiliser and power complexes in:
questions.explanation: The HVJ gas pipeline links Hazira in Gujarat with Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh, via Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh. It feeds power stations and fertiliser plants across western and northern India.

questions.question: National Waterway No. 1 (NW-1), having a navigable length of 1,620 km, is situated on which river system?
options: The Ganga river between Prayagraj and Haldia
The Brahmaputra river between Sadiya and Dhubri
The West Coast Canal in Kerala
questions.explanation: The Ganga river between Prayagraj (Allahabad) and Haldia (1,620 km) is declared as National Waterway No. 1 (NW-1).

questions.question: National Waterway No. 2 (NW-2) spans a length of 891 km on which river in north-eastern India?
options: The Barak river between Lakhipur and Manga
The Teesta river between Jalpaiguri and Rangpo
The Subansiri river in Arunachal Pradesh
The Brahmaputra river between Sadiya and Dhubri
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra river between Sadiya and Dhubri (891 km) is designated as National Waterway No. 2 (NW-2).

questions.question: Why was Kandla Port in Kachchh (Gujarat) developed immediately after Independence?
options: To import crude petroleum exclusively for the Himalayan states
To facilitate naval defense exercises during peace times
To ease the volume of trade on Mumbai port after the loss of Karachi port to Pakistan
To replace Kolkata port as an inland riverine terminus
questions.explanation: Kandla in Kachchh was the first port to be developed soon after Independence to ease the volume of trade on the Mumbai port, in the wake of loss of Karachi port to Pakistan after Partition.

questions.question: Which premier iron ore exporting port of India in Goa accounts for about 50 percent of the country's total iron ore export?
questions.explanation: Marmagao port (Goa) is the premier iron ore exporting port of the country. This port accounts for about fifty percent of India's iron ore export.

questions.question: Which port on the eastern coast of India is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port, originally conceived as an outlet for iron ore exports?
questions.explanation: Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port on the eastern coast. This port was originally conceived as an outlet for iron ore exports from Bailadila mines in Chhattisgarh.

questions.question: Which of the following ports is an inland riverine tidal port that serves a vast and rich hinterland of the Ganga-Brahmaputra basin?
questions.explanation: Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hugli River. Being a tidal port, it requires constant dredging of the riverbed to maintain navigation depth for ocean-going vessels.

questions.question: Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd. provides helicopter transport services primarily to:
options: Private tourist luxury hotels in metropolitan cities
Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) in its off-shore operations and inaccessible areas of north-east India
questions.explanation: Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd. provides helicopter services to Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) in its offshore operations, to inaccessible areas and difficult terrains like the north-eastern states and interior parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Under the Indian postal network, which categories of mail are considered 'First-Class Mail' and are airlifted between stations covering both land and air?
questions.explanation: Cards and envelopes are considered first-class mail and are airlifted between stations covering both land and air. Second-class mail includes book packets, registered newspapers and periodicals, carried by surface transport.

questions.question: A country is said to have a 'Favourable Balance of Trade' when:
options: The value of its imports exceeds the value of its exports
All foreign trade is conducted strictly through gold bullion
The country ceases all commercial shipping with international partners
The value of its exports exceeds the value of its imports
questions.explanation: The balance of trade of a country is the difference between its export and import. When the value of export exceeds the value of imports, it is called a favourable balance of trade.
